title: Geodesics, symmetries and conserved quantities
scope: Curves of free fall and the symmetries that make them solvable. Geodesics as autoparallel and as extremal curves; affine and non-affine parametrization; timelike, null and spacelike geodesics and the normalization of their tangents; variational methods (length functional, quadratic geodesic Lagrangian, free-particle action); maximal proper time, normal geodesics and conjugate points; the geodesic postulate, including forced motion. Lie brackets, Lie dragging and Lie derivatives; isometries, Killing vectors and Killing's equation, adapted coordinates and isometry groups; stationary, static, axisymmetric, cylindrical and plane-symmetric spacetimes; and the conserved energy and angular momentum that metric symmetries give along geodesics. Geodesic deviation, congruence focusing, motion in specific spacetimes, field-theoretic Noether currents and global charges are handled by other domains.

concepts.title: Test particle
concepts.summary: A test particle is an idealized body that responds to the gravitational field but is too small to change it, so the spacetime it moves through can be treated as fixed in advance.
concepts.notes: Needed to state the geodesic postulate cleanly without back-reaction (d'Inverno ch09).

concepts.title: Geodesic
concepts.summary: A geodesic is the straightest possible curve in a space with a connection: its tangent vector is parallel transported along itself, nabla_u u = 0 with an affine parameter. Through each point and in each direction there is locally exactly one geodesic.

names: local existence and uniqueness of geodesics

merged_from: local existence and uniqueness of geodesics
concepts.notes: d'Inverno first defines an affine geodesic with an arbitrary parameter (tangent transported into a multiple of itself) and then specializes; local existence and uniqueness follows from ODE theory, while globally geodesics from one point can meet again (see conjugate-point). Schutz motivates it via Euclid's notion of extending a line.

concepts.title: Affine parameter
concepts.summary: An affine parameter is a parameter along a geodesic in which the geodesic equation has no term proportional to the tangent; any two are related by lambda -> a lambda + b. Proper time (or proper length) is affine for non-null geodesics, while null geodesics need some other affine parameter because proper time does not advance along them.
concepts.notes: Includes the photon convention p = dx/dlambda (Schutz ch11), the observation that without a metric affine length compares segments only on one geodesic (d'Inverno ch06), and the result that a parameter linear in the interval kills the extra term in the metric geodesic equation.

concepts.title: Geodesic equation
concepts.summary: In coordinates a geodesic obeys d^2x^mu/dlambda^2 + Gamma^mu_ab (dx^a/dlambda)(dx^b/dlambda) = 0 with lambda affine; it is a second-order ODE fixed by a starting point and initial tangent. In GR it is the equation of motion of a freely falling particle.

names: geodesic equation from a freely falling frame

merged_from: geodesic equation from a freely falling frame
concepts.notes: Can be derived by transforming d^2xi/dtau^2 = 0 out of a freely falling frame (Gifted Amateur Ex. 8.3). Worked application: if Gamma^i_00 = 0 a particle at rest in the coordinates stays at rest, a quick test for comoving coordinates (Gifted Amateur ch15).

concepts.title: Non-affinely parametrized geodesic
concepts.summary: With a general parameter a geodesic satisfies nabla_u u = f u: the tangent keeps its direction but changes length, and the extra term reflects the choice of parameter, not a force. Being a geodesic is a property of the image curve, and a reparametrization that removes f makes the parameter affine.
concepts.notes: d'Inverno gets f = (d^2s/du^2)/(ds/du) from the variational derivation with arc length s; Gifted Amateur illustrates it with unevenly spaced ticks along a geodesic.

concepts.title: Timelike, spacelike and null geodesics
concepts.summary: Geodesics in a Lorentzian spacetime are classified by their tangent as timelike, spacelike or null. Because a metric connection preserves the tangent's norm along an affinely parametrized geodesic, the character never changes along the curve; in Minkowski coordinates all three are straight lines.
concepts.notes: Spacelike geodesics use proper length as parameter; no physical particle travels on them but they are useful geometric tools.

concepts.title: Normalization of the geodesic tangent
aliases: conservation of u.u along a geodesic
constancy of the geodesic tangent norm
concepts.summary: Along an affinely parametrized geodesic g_ab u^a u^b is constant, so it can be fixed once: -1 for a massive particle parametrized by proper time, 0 for light, and +1 for a spacelike geodesic parametrized by proper length (signs flip in the +--- signature). This first integral is usually the easiest extra equation when solving geodesic problems.

names: conservation of u.u along a geodesic

merged_from: conservation of u.u along a geodesic
concepts.notes: Sign convention causes confusion: d'Inverno writes 2K = +1 for timelike curves in +--- signature, whereas Schutz and Gifted Amateur use u.u = -1.

concepts.title: Null geodesic
concepts.summary: A null geodesic is a geodesic whose tangent has zero norm everywhere, so it runs along the local light cone and has no proper time; it must be labelled with an affine parameter. Freely propagating light follows null geodesics.
concepts.notes: Example from d'Inverno ch23: the gradient of a function whose level sets are null hypersurfaces is tangent to affinely parametrized null geodesics (the generators).

concepts.title: Geodesics as extremal curves
aliases: Euler-Lagrange equations for the length functional
concepts.summary: A curve joining two points is a metric geodesic if its length (or proper time) is stationary under small variations with fixed ends; applying the Euler-Lagrange equations to L = |g_ab xdot^a xdot^b|^(1/2) reproduces the geodesic equation of the Levi-Civita connection. Because the length integral does not depend on how the curve is parametrized, one varies first and only then chooses the parameter to be arc length or proper time, making L = 1.

names: Euler-Lagrange equations for the length functional
reparametrization invariance of the length functional
straight lines as geodesics of flat space
Euler-Lagrange equations for the length functional
metric geodesic as a curve of stationary interval

merged_from: metric geodesic as a curve of stationary interval
Euler-Lagrange equations for the length functional
reparametrization invariance of the length functional
straight lines as geodesics of flat space
concepts.notes: The stationary value may be a minimum, maximum or saddle. Worked checks: straight lines in the Euclidean plane, including the polar form r = a/cos(theta - theta0) (Gifted Amateur ch08). Gifted Amateur warns that setting L = 1 before varying is wrong.

concepts.title: Affine versus metric geodesics
concepts.summary: A manifold with an independent connection and metric has two families of privileged curves: autoparallels, which never change direction, and metric geodesics, which extremize length. They coincide exactly when the connection is the torsion-free metric-compatible Levi-Civita connection, which is why GR can use either definition.

concepts.title: Relativistic free-particle action
concepts.summary: The action of a free massive particle is minus its rest mass times the proper time along its world line, S = -m integral dtau. Its stationary paths are timelike geodesics, the minus sign turns maximal proper time into an extremum of S, and the integral takes the same value for any monotonic parametrization.

names: action for a free relativistic particle
action for a free relativistic particle
rest mass fixed by the Newtonian limit

merged_from: action for a free relativistic particle
rest mass fixed by the Newtonian limit
concepts.notes: d'Inverno fixes the constant by the Newtonian limit. Gifted Amateur later uses it as the template for adding interactions and for the string action.

concepts.title: Geodesic Lagrangian
concepts.summary: With an affine parameter, geodesics of every causal type are the Euler-Lagrange solutions of K = (1/2) g_ab xdot^a xdot^b, which gives the same equations as the square-root length Lagrangian but has no square roots and also works for null curves. Coordinates missing from the metric give conserved momenta at once, and K itself is a first integral.

names: equivalence of the K-Lagrangian and the arc-length Lagrangian

merged_from: equivalence of the K-Lagrangian and the arc-length Lagrangian
concepts.notes: The standard shortcut for Schwarzschild geodesics in d'Inverno ch16-17. Gifted Amateur Ex. 9.9 justifies it: replacing L by a monotonic function of L leaves the affinely parametrized paths unchanged.

concepts.title: Lagrangian method for Christoffel symbols
aliases: reading off Christoffel symbols from geodesic equations
concepts.summary: Write the Euler-Lagrange equations of K = (1/2) g_ab xdot^a xdot^b as xddot^a + (terms quadratic in xdot) = 0; the coefficient of xdot^b xdot^c is Gamma^a_bc when b = c and 2 Gamma^a_bc when b and c differ. For diagonal metrics this is usually much quicker than the Christoffel formula.

names: reading off Christoffel symbols from geodesic equations

merged_from: reading off Christoffel symbols from geodesic equations

concepts.title: Great circles as geodesics of the sphere
concepts.summary: On a unit sphere with metric dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2 the geodesic equations have great circles as solutions, such as meridians and the equator, while other circles of latitude are not geodesics. It is the standard first example of geodesics in a curved space and of geodesics from one point meeting again.

names: great circles as geodesics of the sphere

merged_from: great circles as geodesics of the sphere

concepts.title: Maximal proper time of timelike geodesics
concepts.summary: Among nearby timelike curves joining two events, a timelike geodesic has the greatest proper time (provided no conjugate point lies between them); there is no minimum, because curves close to null zigzags have almost none. The Lorentzian sign reverses the Euclidean statement that geodesics are locally shortest.

names: maximal proper time of timelike geodesics
maximal proper time of timelike geodesics

merged_from: maximal proper time of timelike geodesics

concepts.title: Geodesic postulate
aliases: law of inertia in geometric form
concepts.summary: In general relativity a massive particle subject to no non-gravitational force moves along a timelike geodesic of spacetime, and light moves along null geodesics. It generalizes Newton's first law: gravity is no longer a force but the geometry that decides which world lines are straight.

names: timelike geodesic as free-fall world line

merged_from: timelike geodesic as free-fall world line
concepts.notes: d'Inverno states it as Axioms II(ii)-(iii) and later shows it follows from the field equations. Gifted Amateur ch06 reaches it from the equivalence principle; the timelike restriction is tied to causality (see causality in special-relativity).

concepts.title: Geodesic equation for four-momentum
concepts.summary: Using tau/m as affine parameter turns the tangent into the four-momentum, so free fall reads nabla_p p = 0. The same equation then covers photons, which have a four-momentum but no four-velocity; it is the curved-spacetime version of conservation of four-momentum.

names: geodesic equation in terms of four-momentum

merged_from: geodesic equation in terms of four-momentum
concepts.notes: Gifted Amateur proves it by noting dp/dtau = 0 in a local inertial frame and that nabla_p p = 0 is a tensor equation.

concepts.title: Geodesic equation with an external force
aliases: Newton's second law in curved spacetime
concepts.summary: When a non-gravitational four-force f acts, m(d^2x^mu/dtau^2 + Gamma^mu_ab u^a u^b) = f^mu: the left side is mass times the covariant acceleration an accelerometer reads, and f = 0 gives back free fall. Keeping u.u = -1 requires f.u = 0.
concepts.notes: Gifted Amateur uses it for polar-coordinate mechanics, where the Gamma terms reproduce centrifugal-type terms.

concepts.title: Kinetic-energy metric on configuration space
concepts.summary: Writing a mechanical kinetic energy as T = (1/2) g_ab qdot^a qdot^b makes g_ab a Riemannian metric on configuration space; the Euler-Lagrange equations become a geodesic equation with its Christoffel symbols plus a generalized force. Force-free Newtonian motion is therefore geodesic motion, which shows the geodesic idea is not unique to GR.

concepts.title: Conformal invariance of null geodesics
concepts.summary: Two metrics related by a conformal factor, g' = Omega^2 g, have the same null geodesics as unparametrized curves, and so the same light cones and causal relations. This is why conformally compactified diagrams display causal structure faithfully.

concepts.title: Normal geodesics
aliases: orthogonality of the shortest path to a surface
concepts.summary: Normal geodesics leave a hypersurface along its unit normal. A curve of extremal length (or maximal proper time) from a point to a surface must be such a geodesic meeting the surface at a right angle, since otherwise sliding its endpoint along the surface would improve it.

names: orthogonality of the shortest path to a surface

merged_from: orthogonality of the shortest path to a surface
concepts.notes: Used in the Gifted Amateur account of the singularity theorem (ch50); the focusing results themselves belong to causal-structure-and-singularities.

concepts.title: Conjugate point
concepts.summary: A point Q on a geodesic from P is conjugate to P if neighbouring geodesics leaving P in slightly different directions meet again at Q (a focal point is the analogue for geodesics normal to a surface). Past a conjugate point a geodesic is no longer locally shortest, or for timelike curves locally longest in proper time.
concepts.notes: Model example: geodesics from a point on a sphere reconverge at the antipode. The corner-cutting argument (Gifted Amateur ch50) shows why: once two nearby geodesics cross, a kinked path can be smoothed into a strictly better one.

concepts.title: Lie bracket
concepts.summary: The Lie bracket of two vector fields is the vector field [X,Y] = XY - YX acting on functions, with components X^b partial_b Y^a - Y^b partial_b X^a; the second derivatives cancel. Geometrically it is the gap by which a small loop of flows along X, Y, -X, -Y fails to close.

names: geometric interpretation of the Lie bracket

merged_from: geometric interpretation of the Lie bracket
concepts.notes: Worked example: the normalized polar basis vectors have a non-zero bracket (Gifted Amateur ch03). With a torsion-free connection [u,v] = nabla_u v - nabla_v u.

concepts.title: Jacobi identity
concepts.summary: For any three vector fields [X,[Y,Z]] + [Y,[Z,X]] + [Z,[X,Y]] = 0. Together with antisymmetry it makes vector fields under the bracket a Lie algebra, and it recurs for commutators of operators generally.

concepts.title: Commuting vector fields
concepts.summary: Two vector fields with vanishing Lie bracket can be made coordinate basis vectors of one chart, and their integral curves mesh into 2-surfaces; conversely, coordinate basis fields always commute. A basis field set is therefore a coordinate basis exactly when every pair commutes.

names: loop-closure test for a coordinate basis

merged_from: loop-closure test for a coordinate basis
concepts.notes: Used in d'Inverno ch10 for the connecting vector of a geodesic family, and in Gifted Amateur ch03 to explain why polar unit vectors are not a coordinate basis.

concepts.title: Lie dragging
concepts.summary: Lie dragging carries a tensor along the flow of a vector field X using only the map x -> x + epsilon X that moves each point along its integral curve, with no metric or connection. A vector field that is Lie dragged keeps joining the same two neighbouring flow lines as it is carried along.

names: infinitesimal transformation generated by a vector field
generation of finite transformations from infinitesimal ones

merged_from: infinitesimal transformation generated by a vector field
generation of finite transformations from infinitesimal ones
concepts.notes: Finite flows are built by composing infinitesimal ones, which is why studying generators suffices (d'Inverno ch07). The connecting vector of a geodesic congruence is Lie dragged along the flow.

concepts.title: Lie derivative
concepts.summary: The Lie derivative L_X T measures how a tensor field changes along the flow of X: compare the field actually present at a nearby point with the value dragged there from the starting point, and take the limit. It needs no metric or connection, maps (k,l) tensors to (k,l) tensors, obeys the Leibniz rule, commutes with contraction and reduces to X^a partial_a f on scalars.

names: Lie derivative as generator of a diffeomorphism
Leibniz rule for the Lie derivative
Lie derivative of a scalar function

merged_from: Lie derivative as generator of a diffeomorphism
Leibniz rule for the Lie derivative
Lie derivative of a scalar function
concepts.notes: Identity L_X L_Y - L_Y L_X = L_[X,Y]. Application: fluid continuity and Euler equations as Lie-derivative statements (Gifted Amateur ch39 exercises). Most generally defined through one-parameter families of diffeomorphisms.

concepts.title: Lie derivative of a vector field
aliases: Lie bracket as a Lie derivative
concepts.summary: The Lie derivative of a vector field Y along X equals their Lie bracket, L_X Y = [X,Y]. The first term of the components is the change of Y along the flow; the second corrects for the way the flow itself stretches and rotates a dragged vector.

names: Lie derivative of a vector field
Lie bracket as a Lie derivative

merged_from: Lie derivative of a vector field
Lie bracket as a Lie derivative

concepts.title: Lie derivative of a general tensor
concepts.summary: In components L_X T is X^c partial_c of the components, minus one term T^..c.. partial_c X^a for each upper index, plus one term T_..c.. partial_b X^c for each lower index. The one-form case follows from the vector case and the Leibniz rule, and the rest by repetition.

names: Lie derivative of a general tensor
divergence from the Lie derivative of the volume form

merged_from: Lie derivative of a general tensor
divergence from the Lie derivative of the volume form
concepts.notes: Example: the Lie derivative of the volume form along v is the divergence of v times the volume form, which gives the volume expansion rate of a flow (Gifted Amateur Ex. 37.5).

concepts.title: Lie derivative with covariant derivatives
concepts.summary: For a torsion-free connection every partial derivative in a Lie derivative formula can be replaced by a covariant derivative, because the Christoffel terms cancel in pairs; for vectors L_X Y = nabla_X Y - nabla_Y X. This makes Lie-derivative statements manifestly tensorial.

names: Lie derivative in terms of covariant derivatives
Lie derivative written with covariant derivatives

merged_from: Lie derivative in terms of covariant derivatives
Lie derivative written with covariant derivatives

concepts.title: Lie derivative versus covariant derivative
aliases: why the Lie derivative is not the covariant derivative
concepts.summary: L_X T at a point depends on the derivatives of X there, not only on its value, so it cannot define a rate of change of T in a single direction. A covariant derivative, which does depend only on the direction, is still needed for parallel transport and curvature; the Lie derivative instead expresses symmetry and dragging.

names: non-tensorial dependence of the Lie derivative on the flow field
difference between a Lie derivative and a covariant derivative

merged_from: non-tensorial dependence of the Lie derivative on the flow field

concepts.title: Isometry
concepts.summary: An isometry is a diffeomorphism that carries the metric into itself, so all lengths, angles and intervals are preserved; more generally a map is a symmetry of any tensor field it leaves unchanged. Lorentz and Poincare transformations are the isometries of Minkowski spacetime, and homogeneity and isotropy are statements about isometries.
concepts.notes: Symmetries can be discrete (reflections) or continuous (translations, rotations); only the continuous ones are captured by Killing vectors. A map between two spacetimes carrying one metric into the other shows that two regions are the same geometry in different coordinates.

concepts.title: Lie derivative of the metric
aliases: metric variation under a coordinate change
concepts.summary: (L_X g)_ab = X^c partial_c g_ab + g_cb partial_a X^c + g_ac partial_b X^c, which for the Levi-Civita connection equals nabla_a X_b + nabla_b X_a. It measures how the flow of X distorts distances.

names: metric variation induced by a coordinate change

merged_from: metric variation induced by a coordinate change
concepts.notes: Under an infinitesimal coordinate change x -> x + epsilon X the metric components shift by minus epsilon times this quantity (d'Inverno ch11), which is the gauge freedom used in linearized gravity.

concepts.title: Killing vector field
concepts.summary: A Killing vector field is a vector field whose flow is an isometry, L_xi g = 0: dragging the metric along it leaves the metric unchanged. Each Killing vector encodes a continuous symmetry of spacetime and yields a conserved quantity along geodesics.

names: theorem: Killing vectors generate infinitesimal isometries

merged_from: theorem: Killing vectors generate infinitesimal isometries
concepts.notes: d'Inverno boxes the theorem that infinitesimal isometries correspond exactly to vector fields with L_X g = 0. A Killing vector automatically satisfies the geodesic deviation equation along any geodesic (d'Inverno Ex. 10.5).

concepts.title: Killing's equation
concepts.summary: A vector field is Killing exactly when nabla_a xi_b + nabla_b xi_a = 0, i.e. the covariant derivative of the lowered field is antisymmetric. As a tensor equation it holds in every coordinate system once it holds in one.
concepts.notes: Gifted Amateur first meets it (ch12) as the condition for -T^mu nu xi_nu to be a conserved current.

concepts.title: Coordinates adapted to a Killing vector
concepts.summary: If no metric component depends on a coordinate x^k, then partial/partial x^k is a Killing vector, because the Lie derivative along a coordinate basis vector is just partial_k of the components. Conversely, any non-vanishing vector field can be made a coordinate basis vector, and several Killing vectors can be adapted at once exactly when they commute.

names: Killing vectors from metric independence of a coordinate
Lie derivative along a coordinate basis vector

merged_from: Killing vectors from metric independence of a coordinate
Lie derivative along a coordinate basis vector
concepts.notes: Worked for Schwarzschild (t and phi) and Rindler in Gifted Amateur ch33. Symmetry is visible only in adapted coordinates; generic charts hide it. The DIV ch14 usage (coordinates adapted to a hypersurface) is a different idea and is handed off.

concepts.title: Killing vectors of flat spacetime
concepts.summary: In Cartesian or Minkowski coordinates every Killing vector has the form X_a = omega_ab x^b + t_a with omega antisymmetric, so an n-dimensional flat space has n(n+1)/2 of them. Euclidean 3-space has six (three translations and three rotations); Minkowski spacetime has ten (four translations and six Lorentz generators), matching the Poincare group.

concepts.title: Isometry group
concepts.summary: The isometries of a metric form a group under composition. Its infinitesimal generators, the Killing vectors, form a Lie algebra: linear combinations and brackets of Killing vectors are again Killing, and maximally symmetric spaces have the largest possible algebra.
concepts.notes: Closure under brackets follows from L_X L_Y - L_Y L_X = L_[X,Y]. Spherical symmetry is defined as an SO(3) subgroup with 2-sphere orbits (owned by schwarzschild-geometry-and-stars).

concepts.title: Second-derivative identity for Killing vectors
concepts.summary: A Killing vector obeys nabla_c nabla_b X_a = R_abcd X^d (sign depending on convention), so on a connected manifold it is fixed everywhere by its value and first derivatives at one point. Contracting relates the wave operator of X to the Ricci tensor, nabla^a nabla_a X_b proportional to R_bc X^c, the identity used to build Komar integrals.
concepts.notes: This bound on the number of independent Killing vectors is n(n+1)/2 in n dimensions.

concepts.title: Time-translation Killing vector
concepts.summary: A Killing vector that is timelike (at least far from the source) generates time translations: in adapted coordinates it is xi = partial_t and no metric component depends on t. Far away it coincides with the four-velocity of an observer at rest, which is what makes -p.xi an energy.
concepts.notes: In Schwarzschild it is timelike only outside r = 2M; in Kerr only outside the ergosphere.

concepts.title: Rotational Killing vector
concepts.summary: A spacelike Killing vector with closed circular orbits generates rotations; in adapted coordinates it is eta = partial_phi, expressing that the metric does not depend on the azimuthal angle. A spherically symmetric spacetime has three of them obeying the so(3) bracket relations.

concepts.title: Stationary spacetime
concepts.summary: A spacetime is stationary if it admits a Killing vector that is timelike (at least in an asymptotic region), equivalently a chart in which no metric component depends on the time coordinate. Time-space cross terms g_0i are allowed, so steady rotation is permitted: a uniformly rotating star is stationary but not static.
concepts.notes: With g_0i non-zero, Einstein synchronization shifts time by -g_0i dx^i/g_00 between neighbours and may fail around closed loops, e.g. on a rotating disc (Gifted Amateur Ex. 6.6). d'Inverno ch25 uses stationarity of de Sitter and the steady-state model.

concepts.title: Hypersurface-orthogonal vector field
concepts.summary: A vector field is hypersurface-orthogonal if it is everywhere proportional to the normal of a family of hypersurfaces, X_a = lambda partial_a f. This holds exactly when X_[a nabla_b X_c] = 0; for a Killing vector this condition makes the orthogonal slices a natural time foliation.
concepts.notes: d'Inverno proves necessity for any field and sufficiency only for non-null Killing vectors.

concepts.title: Static spacetime
concepts.summary: A spacetime is static if it has a hypersurface-orthogonal timelike Killing vector; equivalently there are coordinates in which the metric is independent of t and has no dt dx^i cross terms, so it is unchanged under both t -> t + c and t -> -t. Stationary observers then share preferred simultaneity slices.

names: time-reversal symmetry of a static spacetime
residual coordinate freedom in static charts

merged_from: time-reversal symmetry of a static spacetime
residual coordinate freedom in static charts
concepts.notes: Time reversal flips the sign of g_0i terms while leaving time-independent coefficients alone, so invariance forces them to vanish. The static time coordinate, normalized so the Killing vector has unit norm at spatial infinity, is d'Inverno's world time. Because t -> -t is a symmetry, every null geodesic run backwards is again a null geodesic (Gifted Amateur ch24). Static-ness holds only where the Killing vector is timelike (r > 2M in Schwarzschild).

concepts.title: Axisymmetric spacetime
concepts.summary: A spacetime is axisymmetric if it has a spacelike Killing vector whose orbits are closed circles about an axis, so in adapted coordinates the metric does not depend on phi. It is the symmetry that survives when rotation breaks spherical symmetry, as in the Kerr metric.
concepts.notes: The extra discrete symmetry phi -> -phi (azimuthal reflection) excludes rotation and removes all dphi cross terms; Bondi imposes it as hypersurface-orthogonality of the axial Killing vector (d'Inverno ch23).

concepts.title: Commuting Killing vectors
concepts.summary: Two independent Killing vectors with vanishing bracket can be made coordinate basis vectors together, so the metric depends on only the remaining two coordinates. Whether their orbits are closed circles or open lines distinguishes cylindrical from plane symmetry.

concepts.title: Cylindrical symmetry
concepts.summary: A cylindrically symmetric spacetime has two commuting spacelike Killing vectors, one with closed rotational orbits and one generating translations along the axis, so the metric depends only on t and a radial coordinate. It is the setting for exact cylindrical gravitational waves.
concepts.notes: The extra reflection invariance z -> -z, phi -> -phi (whole-cylinder symmetry) removes all dphi and dz cross terms.

concepts.title: Plane symmetry
concepts.summary: A plane-symmetric spacetime has two commuting spacelike Killing vectors whose orbits are both open lines, such as translations in y and z, so the metric depends only on t and x (or null coordinates u and v). It underlies exact plane gravitational wave solutions.

concepts.title: Conserved momentum from metric symmetry
aliases: conservation of momentum conjugate to an ignorable coordinate
concepts.summary: If no metric component depends on a coordinate x^beta, the covariant component p_beta of a freely falling particle's four-momentum (massive or massless) is constant along its geodesic. It follows from the lowered geodesic equation m dp_beta/dtau = (1/2) g_na,beta p^n p^a.

names: conservation of momentum conjugate to an ignorable coordinate
geodesic equation for covariant momentum components
conserved momentum components from metric symmetries
conserved momentum component from metric symmetry
conserved momentum along a cyclic coordinate

merged_from: conservation of momentum conjugate to an ignorable coordinate
conserved momentum components from metric symmetries
conserved momentum component from metric symmetry
geodesic equation for covariant momentum components
conserved momentum along a cyclic coordinate
concepts.notes: Applications: p_0 and p_phi in Schwarzschild (Schutz ch11), p_chi of a radial photon in a homogeneous cosmology (Schutz ch13), and the conserved fifth momentum, read as electric charge, in Kaluza-Klein theory (Gifted Amateur ch48). Only the covariant (lower-index) component is conserved.

concepts.title: Conserved quantity from a Killing vector
concepts.summary: If xi is a Killing vector and u is the tangent of an affinely parametrized geodesic, then u.xi is constant along the geodesic: nabla_u(u.xi) = u^a u^b nabla_a xi_b, which vanishes because Killing's equation makes nabla_a xi_b antisymmetric. In adapted coordinates this is the rule that u_alpha is conserved when the metric does not depend on x^alpha.

names: conservation law from a Killing vector
conserved quantity along a geodesic from a Killing vector
Earn a conserved quantity from a symmetry

merged_from: conservation law from a Killing vector
conserved quantity along a geodesic from a Killing vector
concepts.notes: The particle version of Noether's theorem; the field version (conserved current T^ab xi_b) belongs to action-principles-and-field-theory and matter domains. Gifted Amateur ch22 gives it first as a three-step recipe and proves it in ch33.

concepts.title: Energy at infinity
concepts.summary: In a stationary spacetime E = -p.xi = -p_t is conserved along every geodesic, and it equals the energy that a static observer far away would measure. Locally measured energies differ from it by redshift factors, and where xi becomes spacelike (inside a horizon or ergosphere) E need not be positive.

names: conserved energy in a stationary spacetime
conserved energy constant from time-translation symmetry

merged_from: conserved energy in a stationary spacetime
conserved energy constant from time-translation symmetry
concepts.notes: For a weak field, -p_0 = m + m phi + p^2/2m: rest mass plus Newtonian potential and kinetic energy (Schutz ch07). Per unit rest mass it becomes the specific energy used in orbit problems (orbits-light-and-tests). Frequency ratios in gravitational redshift follow from its conservation.

concepts.title: Conserved angular momentum along geodesics
concepts.summary: In an axisymmetric spacetime the component p_phi = p.eta of a geodesic's momentum along the rotational Killing vector is conserved. For a nearly flat metric and slow motion it reduces to the Newtonian angular momentum m r^2 dphi/dt.

names: conserved angular momentum in an axisymmetric spacetime

merged_from: conserved angular momentum in an axisymmetric spacetime
concepts.notes: The specific angular momentum L-tilde used for Schwarzschild and Kerr orbits is owned by orbits-light-and-tests and black-holes.

out_of_scope_candidates.note: Used to define conserved charges at infinity (Komar integrals) in asymptotically flat spacetimes.
